rows.content: Speculative decoding works by having a small, cheap "draft" model guess several upcoming tokens, then letting the big model check all those guesses in a single pass—so when the draft is right, you get many tokens for the price of one, but when it's wrong, the big model rejects the bad guesses and you fall back to producing tokens one at a time. Counting is a task where the draft model can predict the next token almost perfectly (the sequence is highly constrained and repetitive), so nearly every guess is accepted and you fly through the text. Prose is the opposite: the next word is genuinely uncertain, the draft model's guesses are often wrong, and each rejected guess wastes the checking work and forces a slow one-token-at-a-time correction—so the very mechanism that makes counting fast becomes overhead that makes free-form writing slower than plain generation.
rows.prompt: In one paragraph, explain to a smart non-engineer why a model that is fast at counting can be slow at writing prose when speculative decoding is on.

```python
def knee(rows):
    """Return the concurrency where marginal gain per added stream first drops below 5 tok/s.

    rows: list of (concurrency, aggregate_tokens_per_second) sorted by concurrency.
    Returns the concurrency value at the first step whose (delta agg_tps / delta conc) < 5,
    or None if no such step exists.
    """
    for (c0, t0), (c1, t1) in zip(rows, rows[1:]):
        if c1 != c0 and (t1 - t0) / (c1 - c0) < 5:
            return c1
    return None

# Example:
# rows = [(1, 40), (2, 78), (4, 150), (8, 280)]
# knee(rows)  # -> 4  (marginal gain drops from 38 to 36 to 32.5 tok/s per stream)
```

The case for small studios owning their inference hardware begins with a simple observation: the tools you depend on should not be able to disappear overnight. When a studio routes every prompt through a rented API, its creative process is chained to someone else's pricing page, someone else's rate limits, and someone else's decision about which models remain available. A quiet deprecation notice can strand months of carefully tuned workflows. Ownership turns that fragility into stability.

There is also the matter of cost and cadence. Small teams work in bursts, iterating late into the night on a single shot or a stubborn paragraph. Metered inference punishes exactly that behavior, making experimentation feel expensive and hesitation rational. A modest machine sitting under a desk inverts the incentive: the marginal cost of trying again is nearly zero, so people try again. That willingness to explore is where distinctive work comes from.

Owning hardware also keeps a studio's material close. Scripts, references, and client assets stay on local disks rather than crossing into services whose retention policies are written for someone else's convenience. from typing import Sequence

```python
def binary_search(xs: Sequence[int], target: int) -> int:
    """Return the insertion index of target in sorted sequence xs (bisect_left)."""
    lo, hi = 0, len(xs)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if xs[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid
    return lo

assert binary_search([1, 3, 5, 7], 5) == 2
assert binary_search([1, 3, 5, 7], 4) == 2
```

```python
from collections import OrderedDict

class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache = OrderedDict()

    def get(self, key):
        if key not in self.cache:
            return -1
        self.cache.move_to_end(key)
        return self.cache[key]

    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache.move_to_end(key)
        self.cache[key] = value
        if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
            self.cache.popitem(last=False)
```

```python
cache.put(1, "a"); cache.put(2, "b")
print(cache.get(1))      # "a" (1 is now most recent)
cache.put(3, "c")        # evicts key 2
print(cache.get(2))      # -1

```

```python
import argparse
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass
class Args:
    input: Path
    limit: int


def parse_args() -> Args:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Print the N longest lines of a file.")
    parser.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True, help="Path to input file")
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, required=True, help="Number of longest lines to print")
    ns = parser.parse_args()
    return Args(input=ns.input, limit=ns.limit)


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    with args.input.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        lines = f.read().splitlines()
    longest = sorted(lines, key=len, reverse=True)[: args.limit]
    for line in longest:
        print(line)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

rows.content:
Im kleinen Atelier eines Uhrmachers beginnt der Tag nicht mit Eile, sondern mit Licht. Bevor die erste Uhr geöffnet wird, rückt der Meister die Lampe zurecht, prüft die Pinzette zwischen den Fingern, legt das Lupenglas bereit – kleine Gesten, die den Übergang markieren von der Welt draußen zur Welt der Zahnräder. Der Raum riecht nach Messing, nach altem Öl und ein wenig nach Holzstaub; an den Wänden hängen Regale mit Schubladen, in denen winzige Federn und Schrauben liegen, sortiert nach Größe und Geduld. Hier draußen mag die Zeit in Terminen zerrinnen, hier drinnen hat sie eine andere Konsistenz: Sie wird hörbar, tickend, greifbar.

Das Handwerk verlangt eine Ruhe, die man lernen muss. Wer eine Uhr zerlegt, darf nicht hasten; jede Schraube will mit dem richtigen Druck gelöst sein, jedes Werk mit der richtigen Neigung gehalten. Der Uhrmacher arbeitet oft mit angehaltenem Atem, nicht aus An
rows.prompt: Schreibe einen fließenden Essay ohne Aufzählungen über das Handwerk eines Uhrmachers in einem kleinen Atelier. Auf Deutsch.

A travessia começa antes do sol, quando o rio ainda é uma superfície escura e espessa que parece guardar o frio da noite inteira. O barqueiro chega sem pressa, desamarra a corda com dedos que conhecem o nó de cor, e o barco se desprende da margem com um suspiro de madeira molhada. Não há cerimônia nenhuma nesse gesto, e talvez seja justamente essa ausência de cerimônia que dá ao momento a sua gravidade silenciosa, como se o mundo inteiro estivesse ainda adormecido e apenas nós dois, o homem e o rio, estivéssemos acordados o suficiente para começar alguma coisa.

A água responde ao remo com uma resistência macia, e cada braçada abre no escuro uma ferida que se fecha logo atrás, sem deixar cicatriz. A névoa paira baixa, rente à superfície, e desmancha-se em fios quando o barco a atravessa, de modo que por alguns instantes temos a impressão de estar entrando numa mat
rows.prompt: Escreva um ensaio contínuo em português, sem listas, sobre uma travessia de barco no início da manhã no rio.
